name: jetson_orin_nano_8gb
display_name: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 8GB module as the deployment host
default_mode_source: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5, Platform Power and Performance, Supported Modes and Power Efficiency, table 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB' (docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5): '* The default mode is 15W (mode ID 0)'
processor: 6-core Arm Cortex-A78AE v8.2, 1.5 MB L2 + 4 MB L3 (NVIDIA Jetson Orin technical specifications (nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin))
memory: 8 GB 128-bit LPDDR5 (NVIDIA Jetson Orin technical specifications (nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin))
accelerator_attach: PCIe Gen3 x4 root port (module: 1 x4 + 3 x1 PCIe Gen3, Root Port and Endpoint; NVIDIA Jetson Orin technical specifications (nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin))

departures.p_host: Each end of the power rows rests on its own source. Vendor: the module's average-power budget in the 15W mode, 'VDD_IN Average Power: 15W' (Jetson Linux r36.5, TDP budget table, row 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB'), is p_host's high end; it bounds the module's average power while it works and states no idle or active figure. Peer-reviewed: tsuyuki2026efficient (ICASSP 2026, read in its arXiv version 2603.26145v1, Table 5) measures a Jetson Orin Nano at 15 W power mode at the board's supply input: idle 4.0 W, the low end of p_host_idle and of p_host (an operator drawing nothing beyond idle); its active readings (ResNet 19.9 W, MobileViT-XXS 14.0 W) are the board's under GPU inference, above the module's 15 W budget, so they are not the module's active power. Preprint: the nominals (p_host 11.01 W, p_host_idle 5.685 W) and p_host_idle's high end (5.69 W) stay cao2026vlaulap's, an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2609.18663v2; every page prints 'Preprint'), class stated: the deployment's work is a difference of two readings (p_host - p_host_idle), and only the preprint states both in one setup (module VDD_IN, the 15 W mode), so the nominal pair is never mixed across measurement boundaries. The work's band ends are the cost ends of the difference (U-J2 targeted pass, M1), each a bound across these sources and never one setup: its high end p_host's high (the vendor's budget, 15 W) less p_host_idle's low (the peer-reviewed idle, 4.0 W), 11 W; its low end p_host's low less p_host_idle's high, never below zero (0 W). No vendor or peer-reviewed figure of the module's own active power in this mode was reachable (the module data sheet DS-11105-001 v1.7 timed out at its distributor's host; tek2026measurement, szegedi2026a and giedra2026benchmarking refuse this host; gamage2026realtime, Neurocomputing 2026, Table 6, prints total 6.01-6.71 W and dynamic 2.09-2.55 W in an unstated mode, so it is not used). The preprint's measurement is on the Jetson Orin Nano 8GB Super developer kit at its 15 W mode (cao2026vlaulap pp. 27-28; Jetson Linux r36.5, table 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB Super': the 15W mode runs 6 CPUs at 1497.6 MHz, the GPU at 612 MHz and the memory at 2133 MHz, and the Super configuration's default mode is 25W), read here as the module's own 15W mode (6 CPUs at 1510.4 MHz, GPU 624.75 MHz, memory 2133 MHz, its documented default).

energy_attribution.basis: Owner answer of 2026-10-29, verbatim choice 'Host's work only (Recommended)': the main energy charges the energy the host spends because of the deployment, its active power above idle while it works ((p_host - p_host_idle) x host time) plus every byte over the chip link and through host memory ((e_link_per_byte + e_host_mem_per_byte) x crossing bytes, both directions); host time always adds to latency. The module's idle power is the host's own draw, whether or not the deployment runs: system-level, printed with the whole-system energy as a labelled system line beside the main energy, never in it. p_host is module power (VDD_IN) while the host works, its idle power included, so the work is charged above the idle floor.

p_host.citation: cao2026vlaulap Table 4 p. 28 (VDD_IN module power: CPU, GPU and DRAM, p. 27); NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5, Platform Power and Performance, TDP budget limits, table row 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB' 15W: 'VDD_IN Average Power: 15W' (OC2; 'VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 20W', OC3) (docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5); tsuyuki2026efficient (ICASSP 2026; arXiv:2603.26145v1) Table 5 p. 8: Jetson Orin Nano at 15 W power mode, power at the board's supply input (a 5 kHz measurement board, sec. 5.1): idle 4.0 W
p_host.note: Module power while the host executes: 11.01 W measured on the module at its 15 W mode under an inference workload (CPU and GPU active; a CPU-only host operator draws less, so the nominal is an upper-side reading), low end the idle floor's low end (4.0 W: an operator drawing nothing beyond idle), high end the vendor's average-power budget of the mode (VDD_IN 15 W).

p_host_idle.citation: cao2026vlaulap Table 4 p. 28 (VDD_IN module power: CPU, GPU and DRAM, p. 27); tsuyuki2026efficient (ICASSP 2026; arXiv:2603.26145v1) Table 5 p. 8: Jetson Orin Nano at 15 W power mode, power at the board's supply input (a 5 kHz measurement board, sec. 5.1): idle 4.0 W
p_host_idle.note: The module's idle power at its 15 W mode: low end the peer-reviewed idle at the board's supply input (4.0 W), nominal and high the preprint's resident-model idle at VDD_IN, measured twice (5.69 W, 5.68 W; nominal their mean). It is drawn while the host waits on the chip and on the link; a host that polls for a transfer's completion draws more, which is not modelled.

host_macs_per_s.citation: Arm Cortex-A78AE Core Software Optimization Guide Issue 6.0 (PJDOC-466751330-14665) sec. 3.17 p. 40; NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5, Platform Power and Performance, Supported Modes and Power Efficiency, table 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB' (docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5)
host_macs_per_s.derivation: 8 FP32 MACs per cycle per core (FMLA throughput 2 per cycle on 128-bit Q form, 4 FP32 lanes) x the mode's CPU max 1510.4 MHz: one core 12.0832 G/s (low and nominal: the host dispatches one ComputeOp at a time on one core), all 6 online cores 72.4992 G/s (high)
host_macs_per_s.note: Peak issue rate: a sustained batch-1 kernel below peak is not modelled, so the MAC time is a lower bound on that term (no published sustained FP32 rate of this core was fetched).

t_host_op_overhead.citation: nachin2026executorch Table 1 p. 6; NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5, Platform Power and Performance, Supported Modes and Power Efficiency, table 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB' (docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5)
t_host_op_overhead.derivation: cycles per operator of a minimal two-operator model (mul + add) over the mode's CPU max 1510.4 MHz: an ahead-of-time on-device runtime (ExecuTorch, (75 + 360 + 390) / 2 = 412.5 cycles: 0.273106 us, low and nominal) and an interpreter (PyTorch Mobile, (324,399 + 7,976 + 8,493) / 2 = 170434 cycles: 112.84 us, high)
t_host_op_overhead.note: The source states cycles without its CPU; the cycle counts are read on this core at its clock (an assumption, stated). The per-operator figure includes the tiny operator's own kernel.

t_host_mem_per_byte.citation: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5, Platform Power and Performance, Supported Modes and Power Efficiency, table 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB' (docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5); NVIDIA Jetson Orin technical specifications (nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin); prashanthis2025pagoda p. 25 (energy per memory operation) and p. 22 (bandwidth)
t_host_mem_per_byte.derivation: 128-bit LPDDR5 at the mode's memory max 2133 MHz, two transfers per clock: 16 B x 2 x 2133 MHz = 68.256 GB/s (0.0146507 ns/B, low); sustained at the fraction Orin AGX's LPDDR5 reaches at 2.1 GHz, 103.9 / (204.8 x 2.1 / 3.2) = 0.773065: 52.7664 GB/s (0.0189515 ns/B, nominal and high)
t_host_mem_per_byte.note: A GPU-driven bandwidth fraction; a single CPU core streaming a host operator may reach less, which is not modelled (the high end equals the nominal).

refused.p_host: no published measurement of the module's power in its 7 W mode was found; the mode's 7 W budget bounds it from above only
refused.p_host_idle: no published measurement of the module's power in its 7 W mode was found; the mode's 7 W budget bounds it from above only

e_host_mem_per_byte.citation: prashanthis2025pagoda p. 25 (energy per memory operation) and p. 22 (bandwidth)
e_host_mem_per_byte.derivation: A cross-module proxy: the energy per byte of a memory operation measured on Jetson Orin AGX's LPDDR5 by power regression above the static power (prashanthis2025pagoda p. 25), read as this module's (an Orin module with LPDDR5): 174.7 pJ/byte at memory frequency 2.1 GHz (nominal and high: this module runs its memory at 2133 MHz in every mode), 141.4 pJ/byte at 3.2 GHz (low).
e_host_mem_per_byte.note: It includes the SoC's own data movement, so it bounds the DRAM's share from above; no measurement of this module's own memory energy was fetched.

e_link_per_byte.citation: bae2021a abstract (Semantic Scholar record of doi 10.3390/electronics10010068); neugebauer2018understanding p. 3, eq. (1) p. 4, p. 8
e_link_per_byte.derivation: 1.93 pJ per line bit of one PCIe PHY end (a Gen4 transmitter at 16 Gb/s, every interface, bias and test circuit included) x the line bits one payload byte costs: 8 x 130/128 / (57.88/62.96 x MPS / (MPS + 24)) = 9.2524 (MPS 512), 9.66669 (256), 10.4953 (128): the host's end at MPS 512 17.8571 pJ (low) and 256 18.6567 pJ (nominal); both ends at MPS 128 40.5117 pJ (high)
e_link_per_byte.note: The chip description prices its own end of the boundary (e_dma_per_byte, e_readout_per_byte); the nominal is the host's end, the high end counts both ends for a chip whose figure excludes its PHY. A Gen4 PHY's 16 Gb/s figure read at Gen3 (8 Gb/s), and the receiver end taken at the transmitter's figure: no PCIe receiver figure was fetched. Idle link power (L0, L1) is not priced beyond the module's idle power.

t_link_per_byte.citation: neugebauer2018understanding p. 3, eq. (1) p. 4, p. 8; NVIDIA Jetson Orin technical specifications (nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin) (PCIe Gen3 x4)
t_link_per_byte.derivation: PCIe Gen3 x4: 8 GT/s x 128/130 x 4 lanes = 3.93846 GB/s at the physical layer, x 57.88/62.96 (the data link layer's share) x MPS / (MPS + 24 B) (the 24 B MWr header of eq. (1)): MPS 512 B 3.45856 GB/s (low), 256 B 3.31034 GB/s (nominal), 128 B 3.049 GB/s (high), as time per payload byte
t_link_per_byte.note: Either direction (the link is full duplex; the program's transfers in and out are sequential).

t_link_transfer.derivation: One host-chip transfer's fixed latency: the median 128 B DMA read 529 ns (NetFPGA, low), the PCIe share of a 128 B round trip, about 900 ns (nominal), and two round trips, a descriptor fetch then the payload DMA as the paper's DMA model sequences them (high, 1.8 us).
t_link_transfer.note: Measured on Intel Xeon root complexes, not on this module's root port (a secondary reading); completion by polling (kernel bypass), so no interrupt latency is included.
